subject: ventures/storage-auction-max-bid-calculator
professional: an experienced storage-auction reseller who buys lien-sale units on StorageTreasures, Lockerfox and at in-person lockouts, or a self-storage lien-sale auctioneer; first checks: is the buyer's premium added to the hammer price (bid = budget / (1 + premium)), not taken as a % of resale; does it handle the platform's premium minimum; is sales tax charged by the facility (and waived with a resale certificate) handled; is the cleaning deposit treated as a refundable cash outlay, not a cost; does the removal-window check reflect office/gate hours rather than 48 continuous working hours; are claims about StorageTreasures accurate and fair

evidence.correctness: Ran calculateMaxBid on DEFAULTS (node -e import('./calc.mjs')) and recomputed by hand: net resale 4000 x 0.35 x 0.85 = 1190; cash stack 3x90 + 10x20 + 60 + 2x60 = 650; break-even hammer (1190-650)/1.12 = 482.142857; target-margin hammer (1190 x 0.60 - 650)/1.12 = 57.142857; planned $50 -> 50 x 1.12 + 650 = 706 outlay, 484 profit, 40.67% margin. All match the tool exactly, and an independent check (profit at the returned bid / net = 0.400; profit at break-even = 0) passes. The premium is applied to the hammer price (divide by 1 + p), not subtracted as a % of resale: correct. A second scenario the author did not test ($2,000 retail, 50% recovery, 13% fees, 15% premium, 1 dump load, 6 h, 30% target) matches by hand: 190.43 / 417.39. One wrong output: with the target unreachable but break-even positive (targetMarginPercent 60, plannedBid 0), maxBidAtTargetMargin is clamped to 0, plannedExceedsTarget is 0 > 0 = false, so healthy = true and the page prints 'This planned bid clears your 60% target margin' while the tool's own plannedMarginPercent is 45.4% (calc.mjs:152). Edge case only; core arithmetic right, so 3.
evidence.completeness: Every README feature works end to end: max bid at target margin, break-even bid, rule-of-thumb bid and gap, outlay/profit/margin at the planned bid including premium, cleanout wall-clock vs window, five banners (index.html:66-71, 137-171), share link in the fragment (share.mjs), usage opt-out honouring DNT/GPC (usage.mjs). Three content pages present and linked from the footer (index.html:94). served-copy.mjs: 'no placeholder or retired origin left in llms.txt, sitemap.xml, robots.txt or canonicals'. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' from the subject dir: 66 pass, 0 fail, 0.84 s. Six seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: premium multiple -> 1 caught; premium as (1 - p) instead of /(1 + p) caught; resale-fee cut removed caught; depositAtRisk > -> >= SURVIVED; plannedExceedsBreakEven compared to the target-margin bid instead of break-even SURVIVED; naiveRuleExceedsBreakEven compared to the target-margin bid SURVIVED. 3 of 6 caught. The two flag-routing survivors matter: the break-even vs target-margin split is the product's stated reason to exist (VENTURE.yaml hypothesis 2), yet no test places a bid or naive-rule figure between the two ceilings. No test covers the target-unreachable healthy verdict or the banner state machine.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (188 lines), index.html script (97-213), share.mjs, the four test files. Clean single engine, validated inputs with named errors, the page imports calc and FIELD_IDS rather than restating them (asserted by page.test.mjs:17). Defects: the loss banner branch (index.html:149-152) never hides overbidWarning, so moving a planned bid from between the ceilings to above break-even leaves both 'clears break-even but misses your target' and 'loses $X no matter how the resale goes' on screen; healthy is recomputed in the page (index.html:167) instead of using r.healthy; clamped maxBidAtTargetMargin used in a comparison (calc.mjs:152). Small and fixable.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed: worked-example figures $482.14 / $57.14 / $800 on README, index and vs-bidding-a-flat-percentage (recomputed); buyer's premium 'commonly 10-15%' and that StorageTreasures and Lockerfox charge one (web search 2026-11-19: Lockerfox 15% with a $10 minimum from May 2025; StorageTreasures 15%, 10% for Pro members) though no file cites a source; removal window 24-72 h (StorageTreasures help centre: facilities pick 24, 48 or 72 h from auction close); deposit refundable and forfeitable, bidders can be banned (StorageTreasures help/blog via search); disclaimer and no-warranty on all four pages; no network primitive (usage.test.mjs scans). Not backed or wrong: (1) the cleanout guide says a 10 person-hour unit planned for 2 'still misses' a 48-hour window if the helper cancels (how-long-...html:139, and FAQ line 160 / JSON-LD line 12): solo it is 10 h, inside 48 h by the tool's own model, so the example contradicts the calculator; (2) vs-storagetreasures.html:13,81 says StorageTreasures facilities 'run the auctions themselves, in person or online' and line 31 'live-online formats': not verifiable from any file or source reached (StorageTreasures hosts could not be fetched; search found online and private-seller listings only); (3) 'a guaranteed loss before cleanout even starts' for the $800 bid (index naive banner index.html:145, vs-bidding-a-flat-percentage.html:58,91, README): the $800 hammer costs $896 against $1,190 net resale, so before cleanout the bidder is still $294 ahead; the loss ($356) exists only after the cleanout stack; (4) 'the facility's lock comes off the moment you win' (how-long-...html:52,67) is unsourced and usually wrong in practice (the tenant's lock is cut before the sale for viewing). The vs page is otherwise careful: no figures for StorageTreasures, an explicit non-affiliation line, and it does not disparage the competitor.
evidence.fitness: Walked a reseller's job at a lockout: enter a doorway estimate, recovery, fees, premium, dump loads, hours, holding; read the hammer ceiling and break-even; check the planned bid. That job finishes on a phone in under a minute and is the main value. Gaps a reseller hits quickly: no sales-tax input (Lockerfox says sales tax is paid to the facility; StorageTreasures says the facility collects it unless a resale certificate is shown; README/index.html:72 disclose the omission); no premium minimum (Lockerfox $10 on bids under $70, which is exactly the size of the tool's $50 worked bid: real premium $10, not $6); the cleaning deposit is not in 'Total out-of-pocket at that bid' though it is cash due on auction day.
evidence.domain: The core method (net recovery after fees minus a fixed cash stack, divided by 1 + premium) is what an experienced bidder does, and margin is on net revenue, not markup. Departures: (a) sales tax and resale-certificate exemption not modelled at all, though both major platforms describe tax collected by the facility; (b) premium modelled as a flat % with no minimum, and the 12% default matches neither platform's standard rate (15% on both for non-members); (c) removal window compared with person-hours / crew as if the crew worked continuously (20 person-hours solo vs a 24 h window is 'not at risk'), while facilities restrict access to gate hours and StorageTreasures notes the deposit is refunded only during office hours; (d) deposit forfeiture is flagged but never priced into profit.

defects.what: Sales tax is not modelled: both named platforms say the facility collects sales tax on the winning bid (StorageTreasures: waived with a resale certificate shown to the facility; Texas taxes 80% of premium and deposit), so the ceiling is overstated by the tax rate for a bidder without a certificate; no tax input or certificate switch

Two of the product's core flags are untested at the distinction they exist for: swapping break-even for the target-margin bid in plannedExceedsBreakEven or naiveRuleExceedsBreakEven leaves all 66 tests green (no test puts a bid between the two ceilings); deposit-window boundary also unpinned

Cleanout guide's worked example contradicts the calculator: a 10 person-hour unit planned for 2 'still misses' a 48-hour window if the helper cancels, but solo it is 10 h, well inside 48 h (repeated in the visible FAQ and JSON-LD)
Removal-window check divides person-hours by crew as if the crew works continuously; facilities limit access to gate/office hours, so 20 person-hours solo against a 24 h window is reported as safe

Target margin unreachable but break-even positive: maxBidAtTargetMargin clamps to 0, plannedExceedsTarget compares against the clamp, so a $0 planned bid shows the green 'clears your 60% target margin' verdict while the margin is 45.4%

When a planned bid moves above break-even after sitting between the ceilings, the loss branch never hides overbidWarning, so 'clears break-even but misses your target' stays next to 'loses $X no matter how the resale goes'
Unverifiable claims about a competitor: StorageTreasures facilities 'run the auctions themselves, in person or online' and offer 'live-online formats'; no source in any file
'A guaranteed loss before cleanout even starts' for the $800 rule bid: the $896 purchase is below the $1,190 net resale, so the loss exists only after the $650 cleanout stack
Premium modelled as a flat % with no minimum (Lockerfox: $10 minimum on bids under $70, so the $50 worked bid pays $10, not $6) and the 12% default matches neither platform's standard 15%; uncited
'The facility's lock comes off the moment you win' is unsourced and usually not how lien sales work (the tenant's lock is cut before the sale for viewing)

verdict: A small, clean browser calculator whose core arithmetic is right: the default example's break-even ($482.14) and 40%-margin hammer bid ($57.14), the planned-bid outlay ($706, 40.67% margin) and an untested second scenario all recompute by hand, and the buyer's premium is correctly applied on top of the hammer price (bid = budget / 1.12), not taken off resale. The StorageTreasures comparison is careful and fair (no invented figures, a non-affiliation line), apart from an unverifiable 'in person or live-online' description. It misses the bar on verification and claims: 3 of 6 seeded bugs survive, including both that blur break-even with the target-margin bid, the distinction the product exists for; the cleanout guide's headline example contradicts the tool's own model; and the $800 'loss before cleanout starts' line is wrong. A reseller would also miss sales tax (facility-collected, waived with a resale certificate), the platform premium minimum, and gate hours in the removal-window check. Finished (completeness 3), not at the bar.
